title: Above the Line, Below the Line
vimeoName: 1. Above the line below the Line - EN 3

segments.text: Hello everyone. Today we're going to learn one of the most important ideas in this training.
It is called above the line and below the line. It is very simple but it can change the way you
work, the way you communicate and the way you grow. Over the next few minutes, I want you to
remember just one question. Am I above the line or below the line? That's it. Just one question.
Am I above the line or below the line? Every day something happens. A mistake is made.
A machine breaks. Someone is late. Someone disagrees with you. The situation is the same
but people respond differently. Some people go below the line. Other people stay above the line.
The situation is the same. The difference is how they respond.
Let's start with below the line. When we are below the line, we blame other people.
We make excuses. We become defensive. We stop listening. We complain. We say,
it wasn't my fault. They caused the problem. Someone else should fix it.
Below the line is about protecting ourselves. It is not about learning. It is not about improving.
It is about protecting our ego. Let's repeat that. Below the line, blame, excuses, defensiveness.
Again, blame, excuses, defensiveness. If you remember only those three words,
you've already learned something valuable. Now let's look at above the line.
Above the line is different. Above the line asks, what can I learn? What can I do?
How can I help? Above the line listens. Above the line asks questions. Above the line accepts
feedback. Above the line looks for solutions. Above the line takes responsibility.
Let's repeat those. Above the line asks questions, listen, accept feedback,
take responsibility, look for solutions. Again, ask questions, listen, accept feedback,
take responsibility, look for solutions. These are the habits of people who keep growing.
Imagine two people. The same mistake happens. The first person says, who cost this?
The second person says, how do we fix this? Which person do you think learns more?
Which person do you think earns more trust? Which person do you think becomes a better leader?
The answer is simple. The person who stays above the line. Now here's something important.
Being above the line does not mean you are perfect. Everyone makes mistakes. Everyone
feels frustrated. Everyone goes below the line sometimes. Everyone. The goal is not to be perfect.
The goal is to notice it. The faster you notice, the faster you can move back above the line.
The first step is awareness. Notice where you are. The second step is choice. Choose to move
above the line. The third step is growth. When you repeat this every day, you become better every
day. Let's read them one more time. Below the line, blame, excuses, defensiveness, complaining,
problems. Above the line, responsibility, questions, feedback, listening, solutions.
Remember them. They will help you every day at work, at home, in every relationship.
So before we finish, I want you to remember one question. Whenever something goes wrong,
whenever someone gives you feedback, whenever you make a mistake, stop for a moment and ask yourself,
am I above the line or below the line? Ask it again. Am I above the line or below the line?
Because every time you choose above the line, you become a little wiser, a little stronger,
a little more trusted, and a little more successful. In the next lesson,
we'll learn the first habit of living above the line and how you can start practicing it every single day.
